name: Battle of Khan Younis

sides.name: Israel
sides.strength: 98th Division (paratroopers and commandos), 162nd Division, Air Force fighter and helicopter sorties
sides.casualties: Roughly 100 IDF soldiers killed and hundreds wounded across the operation

sides.name: Hamas and allied factions
sides.commander: Yahya Sinwar (Hamas, presumed local), Mohammed Deif
sides.strength: Estimated 8,000 to 10,000 fighters of the al-Qassam Brigades and allied factions, supported by an extensive tunnel network

victor: Israel (operational control of the surface; underground network only partially neutralised)
summary: After the limited truce of late November 2023 broke down, the Israeli army shifted the main effort south to Khan Younis, identified as the operational headquarters of Hamas's senior leadership. The 98th and 162nd Divisions pushed into the city from the north and the coast, encircled the city center, then cleared neighborhoods block by block through January and February while engineers worked the tunnel system underneath. Israel announced a withdrawal of most ground forces on the seventh of April, leaving a buffer along the corridor it had cut through Gaza.
significance: Khan Younis was the second major urban operation of the Israel–Hamas war after Gaza City and produced the largest displacement of the campaign, forcing about a million people from north and central Gaza into Rafah in the south. The IDF claimed to have killed thousands of fighters and destroyed dozens of tunnels but did not capture Sinwar, who was killed instead in Rafah six months later. Civil-society infrastructure across the city was almost entirely destroyed.
